MMM.rationale: MMM's fundamental health and trajectory are deteriorating sharply. Q1 2026 showed revenue of $6.03B (only +1.3% YoY) but EPS collapsed 39.7% YoY to $1.23, with net income down 41.3%. Operating cash flow plunged 826.6% YoY to just $574M. The balance sheet is strained: total equity has shrunk from $4.52B (Q1 2025) to $3.31B, while total liabilities of $32.12B dwarf equity, implying a debt-to-equity ratio of ~9.7x. Gross margins compressed from 41.7% to 40.8% QoQ, and operating margins fell. The company faces massive ongoing legal liabilities from PFAS and earplug litigation, including a new A$1.4B Australian government lawsuit filed in late May 2026. Valuation is extremely stretched: P/E of 30.6x is at the top of its 365-day range (17.7-30.8), P/B of 25.8x is at the ceiling of its range (17.1-26.0), and net margin has compressed from 17.9% to 11.2%. The stock has rallied +12.5% in the past quarter despite deteriorating fundamentals, creating a dangerous disconnect. Near-term catalysts are negative: the Australian PFAS lawsuit adds fresh legal overhang, inflation is accelerating (headline CPI at 4.2%), and the Fed may need to raise rates, which would pressure industrial demand. Goldman Sachs' upgrade citing 'self-help potential' appears to be a contrarian sell signal given the fundamental deterioration. The combination of collapsing earnings, stretched valuation, massive legal liabilities, and no credible positive near-term catalyst makes this extremely unattractive.
